note: Attacker-controlled pcapng bytes enter the fuzz target
Fuzz input is written to a temporary .pcapng file for the PcapNg reader
PcapNgFileReaderDevice is constructed to parse the crafted pcapng file
getNextPacket is called repeatedly to parse packets from the pcapng input
Calls into LightPcapNg to read the next packet; pktHeader.captured_length is populated from the file
captured_length (uint32_t) is taken directly from the Enhanced Packet Block's capture_packet_length field, which is fully attacker-controlled
Reads the 4-byte capture_packet_length value from the pcapng file; a crafted value like 0xFFFFFFFF is accepted without validation
PADD32 aligns captured_packet_length to 4 bytes; with 0xFFFFFFFF the aligned size overflows and calloc fails or allocates an enormous buffer
memcpy copies captured_packet_length bytes from the file buffer into the allocated packet_data; with a huge captured_packet_length this reads far beyond the input buffer

code: uint8_t* myPacketData = new uint8_t[pktHeader.captured_length]; memcpy(myPacketData, pktData, pktHeader.captured_length);
note: The attacker-controlled captured_length (e.g., 0xFFFFFFFF) is used as the size for new[] and memcpy; the huge size causes ASAN to report negative-size-param or allocation failure
captured_length (uint32_t) is implicitly converted to int rawDataLen; a value above INT_MAX becomes negative, triggering the ASAN negative-size-param error
